# Piaget

**Authors:** Hannah K. Scott, Mark Cogburn

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Jean Piaget (1896-1980) was a renowned 20th-century psychologist and a pioneer in developmental child psychology. Piaget did not accept the prevailing theory that knowledge was innate or a priori. Instead, he believed a child’s knowledge and understanding of the world developed empirically over time through the child’s interaction with the world. His cogitations on cognitive development, in parallel with his epistemological view, gave birth to the study of genetic epistemology. Most famously, Piaget observed how children create schemas that shape their perceptions, cognition, and judgments of the world. He classified the child’s development into 4 sequential periods: 1. The sensorimotor period is from birth through the 1st 18 to 24 months. 2. The pre-operations period is between the ages of 2 and 7. 3. The concrete operations period occurs between the ages of 7 and 11. 4. The formal operations period begins around age 11 and continues through adolescence.
